Return findings DIRECTLY in your final message as dense structured notes. Do NOT write .md files. No code. Target ~700-900 words of pure specifics.

Typography uses Inter for sans, Manrope for headings, Source Code Pro for mono, plus a custom pixel bitmap font for accents. Credibility signals lean on naming Postgres and RLS plus a GitHub star count in the nav rather than hard metrics, and the layout is asymmetric with a two-column grid aligning headline and subhead at the baseline, separated by generous vertical spacing instead of visible dividers.

Now I'm starting to look at render.com's hero section and headline copy.

The credibility signals round out with "7 million builders", a Fortune logo wall, and hardware specs, all set in an editorial grid with literal column rules as separators.

Then hetzner.com: a photographic hero of the actual GEX45 server in a Swiper carousel, pitching Blackwell GPU upgrades with specs like 24GB VRAM and FP4 tensor cores. They run a startPageSwiper carousel plus an A/B testing script on the homepage, with prices injected dynamically into the "Starting at" price slots.

Type is Inter (full weight set), Montserrat, and Hack for mono, confirmed from their fonts.css. Credibility comes from hardware model numbers as headlines, product-grid tiles with live pricing, and a genuine Server Auction with a countdown — framed as a real Dutch auction rather than fake urgency. Layout is a dense product matrix with red accents on white/dark.

Now digitalocean.com: hero reads "AI-Native Cloud" over a cityscape illustration with a styled depth-scale column of numbers (25/50/100...1400) — essentially a nautical depth gauge motif.

Motion includes a 30s linear infinite logo marquee, two 1s entrance keyframes, a springy bounce with a custom cubic-bezier curve, and four `prefers-reduced-motion` guards disabling animation. Type is Inter plus Plus Jakarta Sans for display and JetBrains Mono, confirmed inline. Credibility signals include "80+ models," "12 regions," a named model ("Kimi K3"), and customer logos like character.ai. Layout is a centered hero with full-bleed illustration and a marquee band.

Now looking at planetscale.com: the hero uses ASCII/box-drawing architecture diagrams rendered in monospace text rather than images, plus a Rive animation reference and a manifest.webm file. Motion is minimal, relying on Rive. Typography uses zero webfonts at all — just system font stacks for both sans and mono, with zero font preloads, which feels like a deliberate flex. Credibility claims include "millions of queries per second on petabytes," "70,000 nodes across 20 data centers," NVMe/unlimited IOPS, and a named Tier-0 designation.

Named customers include Cursor/Anysphere, Slack, GitHub, Block, and Bloomberg, with a long-form, nearly document-like editorial layout.

Now for hostinger.com: the hero features an autoplay video from Cloudflare Stream plus Rive, a "Free domain for 1 year" badge, and the headline "Your idea, online. Made easy." Motion includes five Rive references, video, six keyframe animations, and three reduced-motion guards. Typography confirmed as DM Sans and DM Mono, with Noto Sans for internationalization. Credibility signals lean conversion-first with a 30-day money-back guarantee and price anchors, showing lower technical specificity than PlanetScale.

Turning to game hosts: Nodecraft uses Rajdhani 600 for squared display headers paired with Open Sans, a #072E83 blue palette, a lean 114-word hero, messaging like "More than just Minecraft Server Hosting" and "Wake & Play Server," 30% off promo, and Rive motion — overall the cleanest execution of the group. Shockbyte pairs Figtree with Cinzel, a Trajan-style Roman serif that gives it a premium rather than gamer feel, set against #171b29 navy with custom vector Minecraft hero art, though it's wordier at 1,420 words and uses seven emoji. BisectHosting looks like it's shaping up as the cautionary tale of the bunch, piling on six typefaces.

Rounding out the comparison set: ApexMinecraftHosting leans on layered parallax banner art and social-proof avatars with a 40% off badge; PebbleHost is pure price-led simplicity at $1/mo with heavy Trustpilot references; HostHavoc stands out for honestly stating its $12/month price right in the hero rather than hiding it.

Looking at word counts across all these sites, the pattern is becoming clear between premium and budget positioning.

Cheap tells extend to stock 3D server-rack renders, repeated pricing badges, and DDoS/24-7 phrases repeated many times, while premium tells favor a single commissioned illustration or real screenshot, one accent hue on near-black, and specs shown as a few chips rather than dozen bullets. I'm noting concrete aurora/dark examples like Railway's indigo-violet gradient with IBM Plex Serif and train parallax imagery, and Fly.io's serif-mono pairing on violet-600 -- there's a lot to synthesize into a comparison now.

Research complete — 18 sites fetched as raw HTML/CSS (WebFetch's markdown conversion strips design signal, so I pulled source directly and read the font, keyframe, and asset declarations).

## Dev-infra tier

**neon.com** — HERO: type-led H1 "The backend for apps and agents, built to scale on Lakebase Postgres" over a **Rive canvas** (704×878, `data-operate-rive="true"`) plus **five separate `<video muted playsInline preload="none">` panels of real product UI**, stacked as an architecture diagram — posters dated `postgres-database-20260813`, `authentication-20260821`, `compute-20260821`, `storage-20260827`, `ai-gateway-20260814`. MOTION: Rive vector loop + per-panel opacity cross-fades (`duration-200`, default `opacity-0`); headline/CTAs static. TYPE (confirmed, CSS vars): `--font-inter` Inter, `--font-esbuild` **"esbuild"** custom display, `--font-geist-mono` **GeistMono**. CRED: almost no numbers — sells via module names + "NEON IS PART OF THE DATABRICKS PLATFORM" eyebrow. Palette `#00e599` primary / `#34d59a`, ~30 alpha steps of each, on near-black. Whole page = **885 words**.

**supabase.com** — HERO: **nothing but type.** `<h1>` is two `<span class="block">`: "Build in a weekend" / "Scale to millions" (2nd in `text-brand`). No image, video, or canvas in `<header>`. Below it a 12-col bento of product cards each with its own PNG (`/images/index/products/database-dark.png`) + a terminal card (`$ supabase functions deploy`). MOTION: only `animate-fade-in`, `animate-marquee` (logo ticker), Radix `animate-in/out`. TYPE (confirmed): Inter body, **Manrope** headings (`--font-heading`), **Source Code Pro** mono, plus a custom bitmap mono **"Departure Mono Superbase"**. LAYOUT: asymmetric `grid-cols-1 lg:grid-cols-2 items-end` — headline left, subhead right, baseline-aligned. Separation = vertical rhythm (`md:pt-40 md:pb-16`), no rules.

**render.com** — HERO: rotating-word H1 "Your fastest path to production for ___" + a **dotLottie** (`aspect-[630/591]`) on a literal grid of bordered columns (`size-[--column-size] border-l`) — graph-paper as structure. MOTION: every transition ships paired `motion-safe:duration-300` / `motion-reduce:duration-0`. TYPE (confirmed woff2): **Roobert**, **PP Neue Montreal** + **PP Neue Montreal Mono** (class `font-montreal`) — licensed, not Google. CRED: "Trusted by over 7 million builders", Fortune logo, $10K migration credits, 512GB instances.

**hetzner.com** — HERO: **photograph of the actual GEX45 server** (`gex45_web_big.webp`) in a Swiper carousel; copy: "NVIDIA Blackwell GPU, latest-generation Tensor Cores, **24 GB of VRAM**, FP4". MOTION: `startPageSwiper.js` + `abTestingStartPage.js` (they A/B the homepage); € prices JS-injected into "Starting at" slots. TYPE (confirmed `/general/dist/fonts.css`): Inter (18 static weights + `Inter var`), Montserrat, **Hack** mono. CRED: hardware SKUs as headline, dense product matrix, live Server Auction with a real descending-price clock.

**digitalocean.com** — HERO: "AI-Native Cloud" over `cityscape.webp` with a `StyledDepthScale` column reading 25/50/100…1400 — a **nautical depth gauge** as hero graphic. MOTION: `animation:fZRbCh 30s linear infinite` logo marquee; springy `cubic-bezier(0.68,-0.6,0.32,1.6)` 375ms; 4× `prefers-reduced-motion → animation:none!important`. TYPE (confirmed inline): Inter + **Plus Jakarta Sans** + **JetBrains Mono**. CRED: "80+ models", "12 regions", named model (Kimi K3).

**planetscale.com** — HERO: type + **ASCII box-drawing architecture diagrams** (`╔═══╗ Primary`, `▼`, `VTGate`) rendered as live monospace text, not images. TYPE: **zero webfonts** — `ui-sans-serif, system-ui` + `ui-monospace, SFMono-Regular, SF Mono, Menlo`; no font preloads at all. That restraint *is* the brand. CRED: "millions of queries per second on petabytes", "70,000 nodes across 20 data centers", NVMe/unlimited IOPS, Cursor CPO quote, Slack/GitHub/Bloomberg.

**hostinger.com** — HERO: autoplay Cloudflare Stream `<video>` + Rive, badge "Free domain for 1 year", H1 "Your idea, online. Made easy." TYPE (confirmed): **DM Sans + DM Mono** (+Noto Sans i18n). CRED: guarantee badges, not specs. Centered, conversion-first.

**Aurora/dark tier:** **railway.com** — `#13111c` indigo-midnight, violet `#3d2259`/pink `#291839` gradient stage, hero headline in **IBM Plex Serif 54px / -1.96px tracking** with Inter body [font per Fonts In Use/Fudge teardown], parallax train `bg-train-day/dusk.webp` swapping by theme, "100 Gbps". **fly.io** — **Mackinac** (serif) + **Fragment Mono** + **Fricolage Grotesque**; "Computers for agents"; no dashboard shot, just a webp + logo wall.

## Game hosts — what actually separates premium from cheap

| | words/page | typefaces | mono? | countdown | emoji | %-off | review badges |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| ghostcap | **852** | Inter + **Fira Code** | yes | 0 | 0 | 1 | 1 |
| nodecraft | 114 (hero) | **Rajdhani 600** + Open Sans | no | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 |
| shockbyte | 1,420 | Figtree + **Cinzel** | no | 0 | 7 | 0 | 1 |
| apex | 1,344 | Source Sans 3 Var | no | 0 | 0 | 1 | 4 |
| hosthavoc | 866 | Proxima Nova + 4 FA icon weights | no | 0 | 0 | 1 | 4 |
| pebblehost | 1,840 | Montserrat only | no | 0 | 0 | 0 | 11 |
| bisecthosting | **3,688** | **6**: Montserrat+Inter+**Akira Expanded**+Roboto+Geist+Fontello | no | 1 | 0 | 0 | 2 |
| godlike | **3,872** | Gilroy | no | **"03:00:00"** | 3 | 2 | 3 |

Concretely: **GhostCap** is the best-looking newcomer — one `hero.webp`, three spec chips (Ryzen 9950X / USA & Europe / DDoS), no price above the fold, Fira Code as the credibility signal. **Shockbyte's** single premium lever is **Cinzel**, a Trajan-class Roman serif, on `#171b29` navy with commissioned vector Minecraft art. **Godlike** is the textbook cheap stack: countdown clock, "💥 Premium Hosting. Minimal Price. Save 75%!", HostAdvice 4.5/5-from-300-reviews badge, "DDoS" 13× and "24/7" 8×. **Bisect** loads six typefaces including a novelty expanded display (Akira) and a Fontello icon font, plus `parallax/dark/pc-desk-steve-figure.svg` layers and `$2.99/mo` three times.

The pattern, stated plainly: premium = ≤2 typefaces (one of them a real mono or a serif), ~850–1,400 words, one commissioned illustration or one real product screenshot, a single accent hue on near-black, specs as 3 chips, no price and no badge above the fold. Cheap = 5–6 typefaces, ~3,700+ words, stock 3D glowing-server renders, countdown timers, emoji in headings, review-aggregator logos, and DDoS/24-7 repeated 8–13×. Note that **none** of the cheap-looking hosts load a monospace face, while every premium infra site does — mono is the cheapest available credibility lever, and the game-hosting category has entirely ceded it.
